question: What skin layer is damaged in a superficial first-degree burn?
explanation: Superficial burns affect strictly the outer epidermal layer, causing localized redness and mild pain without blistering. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h1)

question: Why are full-thickness burns frequently described as painless at the injury site?

options.A: Edema quickly compresses local sensory nerve fibers
options.B: The body releases massive amounts of natural endorphins
options.C: Cold water first-aid numbs the deep nerve pathways
options.D: Nerve endings in the dermis are completely destroyed

explanation: Complete destruction of dermal tissue ruins the sensory nerve endings responsible for transmitting pain signals. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h1)

question: What percentage of TBSA is assigned to the entire anterior trunk in an adult?
explanation: The anterior trunk covering the chest and abdomen accounts for 18% of the total body surface area in adults. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h2)

question: A patient has burns to the entire right arm and the front of the chest. What is the calculated TBSA?
explanation: The right arm equals 9% and the anterior trunk equals 18%, totaling 27% TBSA. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h2)

question: The primary physiological shift causing burn shock is...

options.A: massive fluid movement from blood vessels into tissues
options.B: excessive production of red blood cells in bone marrow
options.C: sudden blockage of major coronary arteries by blood clots
options.D: rapid electrolyte retention causing severe fluid overload

explanation: Increased capillary permeability causes fluid to leak out of the vascular space, leading to profound hypovolemia. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h3)

question: Why does acute kidney injury frequently threaten patients during the early phase of severe burns?

options.A: Intravenous fluids dilute all essential body electrolytes
options.B: Urinary catheters block normal urine flow completely
options.C: Reduced cardiac output drops renal blood flow sharply
options.D: Direct heat exposure burns the kidneys through the back

explanation: Hypovolemia and lowered cardiac output drastically decrease perfusion to the kidneys, leading to ischemic renal failure. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h3)

question: Which sign strongly suggests a potential inhalation injury in a burn patient?

options.A: Singed nasal hairs and facial burns
options.B: Cold extremities with weak peripheral pulses
options.C: High fever and productive yellow cough
options.D: Dry skin and absent bowel sounds

explanation: Facial burns and soot around the nose or mouth warn of impending airway thermal and chemical damage. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h4)

question: Why is ice water strictly avoided when cooling a fresh burn injury?

options.A: Freezing temperatures permanently numb all local skin reflexes
options.B: Extreme cold causes local vasoconstriction and deepens tissue injury
options.C: Ice melts too quickly and complicates accurate TBSA calculation
options.D: Cold water reacts chemically with exposed subcutaneous fat

explanation: Severe cold causes intense blood vessel constriction, worsening tissue ischemia and converting partial-thickness burns into full-thickness wounds. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h4)

question: How is the total fluid volume calculated using the Parkland formula for an adult burn patient?

options.A: 6 mL multiplied by body weight in kg and TBSA percentage
options.B: 4 mL multiplied by body weight in kg and TBSA percentage
options.C: 2 mL multiplied by body weight in kg and TBSA percentage
options.D: 9 mL multiplied by body weight in kg and TBSA percentage

explanation: The standard Parkland formula uses 4 mL of crystalloid per kilogram of body weight per percentage of TBSA burned. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary clinical parameter nurses use to evaluate the success of burn fluid resuscitation?
explanation: Urine output is the most reliable, sensitive indicator of adequate kidney and systemic organ perfusion during fluid resuscitation. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h5)

question: What type of skin graft uses tissue taken from the patient's own body?
explanation: An autograft involves harvesting healthy skin from an unburned area of the same patient, ensuring permanent acceptance. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h6)

question: Why is early surgical debridement and eschar removal clinically necessary in deep burns?

options.A: It restores normal skin sensation and sweating capabilities immediately
options.B: It eliminates the need for any subsequent intravenous fluid therapy
options.C: It eliminates dead tissue that promotes bacterial growth and infection
options.D: It completely stops all local inflammation and systemic edema formation

explanation: Necrotic eschar is rich in protein and lacks blood supply, making it an ideal medium for rapid bacterial proliferation and sepsis. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h6)

question: The primary metabolic response following a major burn injury is...

options.A: total cessation of protein synthesis throughout the body
options.B: a hypermetabolic state with rapid breakdown of body tissue
options.C: rapid stabilization of basal energy expenditure within days
options.D: profound metabolic slowing with significant weight gain

explanation: Severe burns trigger massive catabolism, rapidly breaking down lean muscle mass and energy reserves to fuel the stress response. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h7)

question: Why is early enteral feeding preferred over parenteral nutrition in major burn patients?

options.A: It preserves gut integrity and prevents bacterial translocation
options.B: It stops the release of cortisol and other stress hormones
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for intravenous access lines
options.D: It is absorbed much faster without requiring active digestion

explanation: Feeding nutrients directly into the gastrointestinal tract maintains mucosal structure and stops gut bacteria from leaking into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h7)

question: What is the most common cause of death in patients who survive the initial phase of a major burn?
explanation: Compromised immune defenses and open wound beds make systemic infection and sepsis the primary lethal complication after initial survival. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of performing an escharotomy on a circumferential chest burn?

options.A: To remove all deep dermal nerve endings and eliminate local pain
options.B: To harvest viable skin grafts directly from the thoracic wall
options.C: To relieve constrictive pressure and restore adequate chest expansion
options.D: To stop the ongoing systemic release of inflammatory cytokines

explanation: Tight, inelastic burn eschar restricts breathing as edema swells underneath; cutting through it relieves the tourniquet effect. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h8)
